findings.evidence: The filter accepts a finite range certificate listing exact products and sums, but its instructions only check that the listed operation results are representable or normal-range. They do not specify checking that each listed result equals the result of the fixed schedule's actual operands, or an inconclusive branch when validation fails. The forward-error bound requires every actual rounded operation to satisfy the zero-or-normal-range hypothesis. If certificate validity is an intended trusted precondition, that is not stated clearly; if certificates are untrusted, this verification is incomplete. Since alg-certified-dyadic-geometric-predicate uses any nonzero filter sign without fallback, accepting an inconsistent certificate could return an incorrect determinant sign.

coverage_note: Reviewed both assigned pages and all 27 assigned items in dependency order, plus the predicate supplier chain and published real-interval prerequisites used by those consumers. The range-certificate issue is marked as suspected because the wording may intend certificate validity as an input precondition. I did not audit unrelated complex-ball and square-root branches or all their transitive suppliers for the general outward-rounded theorem.
